model_outputs: We can solve all of these problems in polynomial time, but the fastest known algorithm for each of them is different. The fastest known algorithm for finding a longest path in an undirected graph is Dijkstra's algorithm, which runs in O(|V| + |E|) time, where |V| is the number of vertices and |E| is the number of edges. The fastest known algorithm for finding a longest simple cycle in an undirected graph is the Ford-Fulkerson algorithm, which runs in O(|V| * |E|) time. The fastest known algorithm for finding all Hamiltonian cycles in an undirected graph is the brute-force approach, which has a time complexity of O(|V|!) and is not practical for large graphs. The fastest known algorithm for finding a largest clique in an undirected graph is the brute-force approach, which has a time complexity of O(|V| * |E| * log |V|) and is not practical for large graphs. The fastest known algorithm for finding a minimum vertex cover in an undirected graph is the brute-force approach, which has a time complexity of O(|V| * |E|) and is not practical for large graphs. The fastest known algorithm for finding a maximum independent set in an undirected graph is the brute-force approach, which has a time complexity of O(|V| * |E|) and is not practical for large graphs. The fastest known algorithm for finding a minimum dominating set in an undirected graph is the brute-force approach, which has a time complexity of O(|V| * |E|) and is not practical for large graphs. The fastest known algorithm for finding a maximum clique in an undirected graph is the brute-force approach, which has a time complexity of O(|V| * |E| * log |V|) and is not practical for large graphs. The fastest known algorithm for finding a shortest cycle in an undirected graph is the brute-force approach, which has a time complexity of O(|V| * |E|) and is not practical for large graphs. question:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite directed acyclic graph with |E| > 0. Which of the following must be true?
I. G has a vertex with no incoming edge.
II. G has a vertex with no outgoing edge.
III. G has an isolated vertex, that is, one with neither an incoming edge nor an outgoing edge.
options: I and III only
None of the above
I and II only
II and III only
I, II, and a vertex with one outgoing edge
I, II, and a vertex with one incoming edge
All of the above (I, II, III)
II only
I only
III only
model_outputs:
I. A directed acyclic graph (DAG) with more edges than vertices must have at least one vertex with no incoming edge. This is because a vertex with no incoming edges is a sink, and a DAG cannot have more sinks than vertices. So, I is true.

II. A DAG with more edges than vertices must also have at least one vertex with no outgoing edge. This is because a vertex with no outgoing edges is a source, and a DAG cannot have more sources than vertices. So, II is also true.

III. An isolated vertex is a vertex with neither an incoming edge nor an outgoing edge. Since a DAG has no isolated vertices, III is false.

Therefore, the correct answer is (A) I and III only.
